campaigns.title: Help Sandip rescue and care for abandoned elderly left to beg on the streets. Donate now
campaigns.description: “I never imagined I would have to sleep at the bus stand despite having an able-bodied son. I was a building contractor, and it was all fine till the time I was earning well. But as soon as I lost my leg in an accident, I came on the streets. My son assaulted me and deserted me,” recalls Laxman Parasram Ajrekar, a beneficiary of Jeevan Anand Sanstha’s home for elderly, a sanctuary for over 230 seniors like him.Over the last decade Sandip Parab and his NGO Jeevan Anand Sanstha, despite facing financial hardships himself, have been a saviour for over 3,000 elderly.  With your support, Sandip can continue to rescue the elderly parents who are abandoned by their own children and give them the love and care they deserve. Donate nowDonate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India), & 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code (USA). A fate worse than death“Just imagine the plight of an elderly mother who, despite coming from a well-to-do background is compelled to live the life of a beggar on city streets. The condition of elderly women who have been abandoned by their children is the worst because they face so many problems and threats on the streets. They lie starving on the streets with festering wounds and incapable of even moving,” says Sandip while talking about the pain of homeless seniors. Sandip has made it his life’s mission to protect and care for such senior citizens and has resolved never to rest till he can reach every elderly who is in need. The only hurdle Sandip faces is that of funds. Your support can enable him to reach countless more senior citizens who have been abused and abandoned by their families.How your donations helpSuch has been Sandip’s resolve to save the elderly from the streets that he has been rescuing them on his two wheeler. Today he faces a huge challenge in providing rescued senior citizens nutrition and medical care. “I treat each and every person at our home for elderly as my own parents. I do everything for them from bathing and cleaning to feeding them. But the problem I am facing is that the number of elderly at our home is increasing with each passing day. I need support in getting rations and medicines for this family of mine” shares Sandip.“When I was in my 20s, I found an elderly person lying unconscious near a railway station. I took him to my friend's home, cleaned him, bathed him and began taking care of him. I later found out that he was the principal of a school. His son was a professor but despite that he had been lying on the road. It is for helpless seniors like these that I decided that I will dedicate my life to care for them.Join this mission to protect vulnerable and helpless senior citizens who are in urgent need of medical care, food and shelter. Donate nowDonate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s largest online donation platform, to support Jeevan Anand Sansthan and other NGOs working in this cause to further their mission of rescuing abandoned elderly from the streets and giving them a loving home.

campaigns.title: Loving mother to 180 blind kids, visually impaired Veena needs your support in caring for them
campaigns.description: “A blind child is seen as a curse or as a burden to the family. These children are left on the street. I have picked up children from roadsides myself. I also lost my eyesight as a child but today I am a senior officer in a public sector company. What would I have done, had I not been taken care of?” asks Veena Mehta Verma who was once a beneficiary of National Association for the Blind, Delhi (NAB) and now works with the NGO to protect and care for blind children like herself.Today, hundreds of blind children supported by NAB, Delhi have found something that they never had before–hope for a better tomorrow. Without Veena and NAB, many of these children would be at the risk of going back to the streets or spend a life of neglect and even abuse. Your support to the NGO is crucial. Donate generouslyDonate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).A life of uncertainty and sufferingEven if a blind child is not abandoned they are often trapped in their homes deprived of education or any way of making a living. According to the nonprofit leader, “For a blind kid, employment is impossible without education. The (blind) kids need to learn Braille or they need ‘talking computer’ aids. Many of these kids are deprived of such facilities”.  Illuminating young lives “At NAB Delhi there are around 200-250 blind kids. There are around 180 kids in the hostel of NAB. We teach Braille, we teach arithmetic Taylor frames. To work towards a brighter future for the blind, we need your support. Please come forward and donate towards our mission”, says Veena. Students for whom NAB Delhi has cared for are today placed in some of the most prestigious organisations across the world. While some have gone on to make a name for themselves in the corporate world, others have taken up art and music as a profession too. Many blind children are bright, academically gifted, and waiting to shine, all they need is an opportunity. And your donation can give them just that.Donate to this fundraiser on Give.do, India’s largest and most trusted online donation platform, to help the blind children get shelter, education, care and a shot at a future full of opportunities.

campaigns.title: URGENT!! People of Assam need urgent help as floods leave lakhs in need. Donate now
campaigns.description: People of Assam need urgent help as floods leave lakhs in need. Donate nowFloodwaters have once again ravaged the beautiful land of Assam, leaving a trail of destruction in its wake. According to the latest reports by the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), over six lakh people have been severely affected by floods across Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, Sivasagar, and other districts. The number of victims of the natural disaster has climbed to over 70, while thousands remain stranded without help. Together, let us rise and make a difference by contributing to our fundraising campaign for the flood victims of Assam.Charaideo is the worst-hit district with nearly 1.9 lakh people affected, followed by Sivasagar (over 1.5 lakh) and Jorhat (around 1.4 lakh). Nestled in the northeastern part of India, Assam has a long-standing history of facing nature's fury. Just last year, the state witnessed a devastating flood that uprooted the lives of countless individuals. This year, the floods have struck again, plunging numerous families into unimaginable chaos and distress. Many have been displaced from their homes, left without shelter, and robbed of their basic necessities.Embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure have also been damaged by flood waters. The urgent need for assistance:In times like these, it is our duty to extend a helping hand to our fellow human beings who are facing the wrath of nature. Your generous donations will directly support our on-ground NGO partners who are tirelessly working to provide immediate relief to the flood-affected people in Assam. The funds raised will be utilised to provide them with essential supplies such as food, clean water, and medical care, bringing hope and solace to their lives during this moment of crisis.The power of your donations:Every rupee contributed to this fundraising campaign will create a ripple effect of positive change in the lives of those who need it the most. Your support will help in:Immediate Relief: Ensuring that the affected families receive immediate assistance in the form of food, clean water, and essential supplies.Medical Care: Providing medical aid to those injured or suffering from waterborne diseases, ensuring their well-being in the aftermath of the disaster.Shelter and Rehabilitation: Assisting in the construction of temporary shelters and facilitating the process of rehabilitation to help affected families rebuild their lives.Here's how your donations can help:a) A food kit comprising essential supplies can be provided for ₹1,255. b) A hygiene kit with essentials for an entire family during floods can be ensured for ₹1,035. c) Our NGO partner can provide temporary shelter for flood-affected families for ₹2,570.Now is the time to unite and show our solidarity with the people of Assam. By donating to our fundraising campaign, you are not just providing immediate relief; you are also offering hope and strength to those who have lost everything. Together, we can make a difference and rebuild the lives of the flood-affected communities in Assam. Join us today and let compassion guide our actions.

campaigns.title: Impart training under SDTP for ST youths
campaigns.description:
Large number of youths from poor tribal sect across Wayanad after mere matriculation is seen wandering jobless. Because of abject poverty combined with lack of consciousness and geographical barriers that created inhibitive environment in societies chronically plagued by mass deprivation and starvation, but they have their own talents in many extra-curricular activities. 
 The chances of getting job on simply having academic qualification now a day’s becomes very difficult, Vocational education in Wiremen & Plumping and Tailoring & Embroidery under SDTP is also mainstreamed here to improve the employability which will also help to meet the growing need for workers with specialized vocational skills. The training now imparted here for matriculated tribal youths of having age of 18 years and above. 
 Each training is now accommodated 30 members for a period of 3 months Wiremen & Plumping and 6 months for tailoring & Embroidery will be provided with certificate on completion of the training which may be used for seeking employment in private/public seek as well as to obtain license to start self employment etc.

campaigns.title: Support Women and Children to access Good Healthcare!
campaigns.description: Every child deserves a healthy start in life. And every woman deserves access to quality healthcare. In India nearly 35,000 women die every year due to pregnancy and child-birth related complications. 57% Women of reproductive age (15-49 years) are estimated to be anaemic.33% of the disease burden among adults (young parents or to be parents) in India is attributed to unhealthy habits during adolescenceGlobally 1 in 3 women and girls are affected by violence and 32% of ever-married women in India have reported partner violence. Rapid urbanisation and overburdened infrastructure creates low accessibility and affects quality of health and nutrition services in urban informal settlements. Most of the above issues are preventable and are mainly due to the lack of awareness of healthy practices and poor access to quality healthcare services.Source: National Health Family Survey-5, World Health Organization 2017It is said that the health of the child and family begins with a woman. If the woman adopts healthy practices the family will also remain healthy. SNEHA’s intervention primarily focuses on women and to bring in behavior change leading to a lasting impact. While doing so we understand there are various factors impacting the health of women and children and hence we have designed a holistic intervention that focuses on the following:Identifying pregnant women at an early stage and supporting them in accessing antenatal, perinatal and postnatal services from healthcare providers to ensure that they deliver safe and healthy babies.Working with children in the age group of 0-6 years to improve infant and child feeding practices, uptake of immunisation and illness management.Counseling caregivers and decision-makers in the family on the importance of balanced diet, dietary diversity and healthy practices to ensure good health of the woman and child.In the communities we work in generally, the husband/father is the decision maker in the family. We work towards making men an active support system for improved health of the women and children in their family and the community.Supporting the healthcare providers i.e. the health posts and public hospitals by helping strengthen their services and bridging the gap between them and the community, to improve the delivery of services.    We provide counseling services to women undergoing violence or depression and also support them with medical or legal help as required by them.SNEHA is a step towards bridging the health equity gap amongst people living in urban poverty, with a special focus on women and children. Significant Progress so far:48608 Pregnant women with potential complications assisted through referral networks (2016-22)8160 Youth reached through life-skills and health education programmes (2016-22)24420 Survivors of violence counselled for psycho-social support and advanced mental health counselling (2016-22)4765 Mumbai Police personnel trained to respond to survivors of violence (2016-22)86% survivors of violence accessing counselling services reported a reduction in violence and distress levels (2021-22)99% of antenatal care clinics functional in project areas The following story of Saba reflects the challenges faced by women and families in the communities where we work, as our on-ground staff provides information and counseling to change behaviours and attitudes to improve the health of vulnerable women and children. Changing minds through careSaba was three months pregnant when SNEHA’s field staff member met her during the door-to-door visit. Already under treatment for white discharge and irregular menstruation related issues at a nearby hospital, Saba was also found to be mildly anaemic at 10.5 g/dl.We faced stiff resistance from Saba’s husband, because of which we were unable to reach her as Saba delivered in the seventh month of pregnancy. The baby was kept in a glass incubator and when discharged from the hospital after 10 days, he weighed 1.3 kg.During the home visits following the delivery, our field staff member educated Saba about food, health and nutrition practices such as kangaroo mother care, exclusive breastfeeding and maintaining hygiene to ensure better health for the mother and child.We continued with anthropometry of the baby which indicated improvement in height (57.3 cm) and weight (4.36 kg) measurements. When her husband saw his child’s progress, he was convinced of the benefits of SNEHA’s interventions.Our continued efforts have shown positive results with the child now shifted to the normal category and the family continues to follow healthy practices to ensure the well-being of the mother and child.

campaigns.title: Run4Retinoblastoma: A fundraiser by Kaustubh Mulay, Dr.Santosh G.Honavar and Ashrita Datta for children affected by retinoblastoma.
campaigns.description: Retinoblastoma is a life-threatening eye cancer that affects children under the age of 6 years. Over 90% of these children are from the developing countries; In India, 5 children develop retinoblastoma everyday. Early and appropriate treatment provides >98% life salvage and 90% eye salvage. However, in regions with poor facilities and delayed treatment, about 80% succumb to the disease. Kaustubh Mulay, Dr. Santosh G.Honavar of the National Retinoblastoma Foundation and, Ashrita Datta with her team at Tonabolic are raising funds for Iksha Foundation to help create awareness and provide aid for treatment of children with retinoblastoma. Your support would immensely help in mitigating the suffering of these children and their families. We urge you to generously donate and help us save these children.Let them live; Let them see.Let's together Run4Retinoblastoma

campaigns.title: KERALA DISASTER RELIEF
campaigns.description: Many states in India are battling floods and Kerala is especially affected with over 50,000 people needing immediate help. There is an urgent need for civic participation to bring timely relief to them. For the last two decades, Goonj has been deeply involved in disaster related work across the country. It has an existing network of communities and partners that are active throughout the year in areas of rural development. At the time of disaster, this network is intensified as a powerful tool of change.Through the initiative “Rahat Floods”, Goonj channelizes this network to bring specific immediate relief kits to flood affected communities and then after a few weeks provides continued assistance and long-term rehabilitation. Urban masses join the effort with both material and money contributions.This year again, with the massive damages and loss of lives, there is a dire need for monetary funds to cover logistics, and material contributions. Goonj's Team headed by founder Anshu Gupta is in the field assessing the situation and is setting up relief operations the way it has done in the last twenty years. First, Goonj will address the basic urgent needs of the flood affected communities. Later in the rehabilitation process, through the initiative "Cloth For Work" material kits will motivate and trigger local communities to action and restore infrastructure like roads, schools, dams etc. and rebuild lives along with way. The affected communities are not mere passive recipients but collectively work with us as an equal stakeholder - be it in assessing the critical situation or in the decision-making.UpdatesThe situation is changing fast and now with all the 14 districts affected. Goonj has initiated action in the districts of Alappuzha, Idukki, Malappuram, Palakkad, Kannur and Wayanad and further expansion is in process. Currently most of the inward and outward transport is blocked but will clear in next few days and this time is being used to collect resources. As on date  trucks have started moving from centers in Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai and based on distances and material available, movement from other major offices like Delhi, Rishikesh and Mumbai will take place.Initial target is to reach out to about 30,000 families in the next few months which will increase as Goonj’s operations grow in Kerala and as more and more resources are gathered. To start with, the focus will be on providing relief kits to families and then to run interventions in schools, aanganwadis & welfare centers.To make sure no duplication of effort takes place, the focus is to try and fill the gaps in the areas where others have not reached or where people still need basic relief. One of the major focus is going to be on tribal population.A typical kit will have a few kg of dry ration, some utensils, tarpaulin, mats, blanket and other essentials like sanitary pads, slippers etc.  Clothing will happen as per need and acceptance. Goonj will also be focusing on other states also which are affected this monsoon including parts of karnataka and tamilnadu.   As on date fund requirement stands at about INR 10 crore for the operation. As our expertise and work is also around mobilizing material, the cost of the kit comes down in our case. Break up of fund requirement is as below: Outreach to 30000 Impacted Families (Including logistics)   =  9.00 crInstitutional needs (Schools, Health centers)                          =  1.00 crTotal                                                                                                =  10.00 CRYour monetary contributions will help Goonj cover the crucial logistics  in reaching relief materials and to purchase basic  essentials in large quantity. Over the years, Goonj has brought significant behavioral changes in the culture of giving where focus has shifted to 'Dignity" from "Charity". Comprehensive disaster relief kits called  "RAHAT Kits" are given to the affected communities and they act as a catalyst in the dignified relief and rehabilitation process. Furthermore, the communities are key players in the decision making and rehabilitation process. They participate equally in reviving and restoring their life back to normalcy. And so a sense of ownership is instilled within them even amidst grave disaster and havoc.
